t: A fast, cheap dual-core RISC-V chip with built-in USB 3.0 and Ethernet.
steps: Buy a MuseLab nanoCH32H417 on Tindie or the WCH evaluation board from AnalogLamb.
Download the example code from the openwch ch32h417 repo on GitHub.
Connect the board over USB-C. The nanoCH32H417 has a built-in debugger.
Open a GPIO blink example and flash it.
Try a USB or Ethernet example next.
Explore the ch32fun examples or Zephyr for an open toolchain.
meta: Open Board. From $17. A few stores.
